reason: E1 directly supports all key premises by reporting that chemical heterogeneity in CoCrFeNi nanopillars causes SFE variations, which coordinate twinning and slip to achieve ~110% uniform elongation and delay necking. E3 provides only tangential support regarding <110> orientation and twinning in a different context (SLM processing). E2 is cited as conflicting but addresses creep at high temperature, not dynamic room-temperature behavior, and does not contradict the premises.
premises: Atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity in HEAs causes wide local variations in stacking fault energy (SFE).
Local SFE variations promote synergistic activation of dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
This synergistic activation delays strain localization and necking, enabling high uniform ductility under dynamic loading.
The effect is demonstrated in <110>-oriented single-crystalline CoCrFeNi nanopillars at room temperature.
